requirements.title: oc resolves bare project-name arguments under ~/dev with deterministic precedence
requirements.body: When invoked as `oc <token>`, the wrapper must preserve existing subcommand/path behavior while resolving a bare token to `~/dev/<token>` or a single `~/dev/*/<token>` match. Ambiguous nested matches must fail with a disambiguation list, and unresolved tokens must pass through unchanged.

scenarios.title: Subcommand and explicit-path precedence remain intact
given: matching project directories may exist under ~/dev
scenarios.when: the launcher resolves the first positional argument
then: the first argument is forwarded unchanged

scenarios.title: Single nested match resolves with notice
then: argv[1] is rewritten to the matched absolute path
a one-line resolution notice is emitted to stderr

scenarios.title: Ambiguous nested matches fail safely
then: a disambiguation list is printed to stderr

requirements.title: openchad exit closes only its own oc-* session when the last client detaches
requirements.body: Each openchad launch creates one isolated `oc-<epoch>-<pid>` tmux session and must configure teardown so only that session is destroyed when no clients remain. The launcher must never invoke `tmux kill-server`, must not affect non-`oc-*` sessions, and must preserve `oc attach` / `oc switch` semantics including multi-client safety.

scenarios.title: Scope is limited to current openchad session
given: other tmux sessions (including non-`oc-*`) may already exist
scenarios.when: the openchad client exits and no clients remain attached to that session
then: only the current `oc-<epoch>-<pid>` session is closed
no other tmux sessions are terminated

scenarios.title: Launcher uses session-scoped teardown command path
given: launcher created a new tmux session for opencode
then: teardown is configured through a session-targeted tmux option path

scenarios.title: Two attached clients do not cause premature teardown
given: two clients are attached to the same `oc-*` session via `openchad` and/or `oc attach`
then: the session remains alive while at least one client stays attached
session teardown occurs only after the last attached client detaches

scenarios.title: Attach and switch workflows remain available
then: no automatic teardown is triggered by listing or switching operations
